A contemporary newspaper identifies William Knox Chandler as an OSS employee on leave from an associate professorship at Vanderbilt, while an official National Park Service history independently identifies Knox Chandler as a former journalist and college professor serving as chief instructor at an OSS Secret Intelligence finishing school. The uncommon Knox name, one transposition in the indexed surname, direct OSS context, and matching occupation support a high-confidence identity.
